why: UNESCO AI Readiness Assessment for STP, produced with the Government, states there is no national AI strategy and no AI-specific law and sets a roadmap action to approve one
UNESCO published the STP AI country profile on 2026-01-22, the most recent dated authoritative statement that no national AI strategy or governance structure exists
UNDP began a two-day AI and digitalisation training for the public administration on 2026-04-21, financed by KOICA; a distinct preparatory step short of adopting a strategy
STP has no standalone broadband strategy; Resolucao 35/2020 in Diario da Republica I Serie n. 60 is the approved national digital strategy that frames connectivity
World Bank ISR of 19 September 2025 records the Law on Electronic Communications and Law on Regulatory Authorities approved by the Council of Ministers and awaiting the National Assembly
AGER provisionally authorised CST to run IPTV over CST ON by Resolucao n. 003/CA/AGER/2026, a distinct national regulatory decision diversifying electronic communications services
The National Interoperability Framework document itself, QNI v0.1 of November 2021, published by INIC with UNDP and UNU-EGOV
Interoperability platform linking the civil registry SIGA and Bilhete de Identidade databases to the electoral roll, presented on 4 September 2025
World Bank ISR records government systems connected to the interoperability platform at 0.00 on 19 September 2025 against a target of 5 by May 2027, and the solution as not operational
INIC states that it is an imperative for security and sovereignty that the vital information and systems of the country be hosted in national territory; the clearest localisation position found
ANPDP records that international data transfer was named a priority working-group theme at the first Rede Lusofona de Protecao de Dados meeting of 26 August 2025
No standalone cloud policy exists; the approved national digital strategy annexed to Resolucao 35/2020 names a Centro de Dados Governamental to consolidate fragmented computing resources
The INIC data strategy and roadmap of July 2025 carries an open data portal as roadmap action 3.1.2, that is as still to be delivered rather than in place
CIPSTP published a citizen budget for 2026 built from Lei n. 3/2026 as published in Diario da Republica n. 18; civil-society reuse of official budget data inside the window
STP has no access to information statute; Artigos 29, 74 and 76 of the Constitution are the whole of the national legal guarantee and create no request procedure or oversight body
The UNESCO AI Readiness Assessment for STP states there are no laws or regulations specific to the development, use or deployment of AI, and recommends a future Lei da Estrategia Nacional de IA
Full text of Lei n. 15/2017 Lei sobre Cibercrime as published in Diario da Republica n. 147 of 6 October 2017; the statute itself, not a summary of it
AGER put the Estrategia Nacional de Ciberseguranca and its action plan out to 30-day public consultation; already staged by a sibling slice, cited not restaged
Lei n. 17/2018 Regime Juridico do Sistema Nacional de Pagamentos is the central payments statute; already staged by a sibling slice, cited not restaged

STP has no e-commerce, e-transactions or electronic signature law; the national digital strategy published in the Diario da Republica lists Legislacao de Instituicao de Assinatura Digital among pending legislative objectives
Records the Lei de Assinatura Electronica approved by the Council of Ministers and submitted to the National Assembly in September 2025; already staged by a sibling slice, cited not restaged
Full text of Lei n. 5/98 Bases do Sistema Estatistico Nacional, the statute that defines the SEN and creates the INE in Artigo 7
